summary: Fix the findings the adversarial pass refuted: erasure, retention, the scans, the email escape hatch, and the billing race

fix.summary:
Both findings are now mechanism, not paperwork.

privacy-legal-03: `MembersService.erase()` exists and `POST /t/:slug/members/:id/erase` (owner/admin only) reaches it. It tombstones every direct identifier on the member row (memberNumber → `ERASED-<16 chars of the id>`, fullName/sortName → `[erased]`, searchText → '', email/phone/dateOfBirth/address*/country/photoAssetRef/staffNotes → NULL, customFields → {}), deletes the photo FILE from the storage volume, strips `notes`/`customFields` on every Loan/Reservation/Fine plus `Fine.reason`, redacts the identifier payloads out of the tenant `audit_log` (both the (targetType='member', targetId) rows and any row whose JSON contains the address), and deletes control-plane `email_outbox` rows addressed to them. WHAT SURVIVES, deliberately: the member row itself as a non-identifying stub (Loan/Reservation/Fine all have `onDelete: Restrict` FKs — a hard DELETE would take the library's circulation history with it or be refused by Postgres); loan history (dates, copy, staff); fines as FINANCIAL facts only (amount, currency, status, timestamps, loan link — Art. 17(3)(b)); row timestamps; and one `member.erased` audit row carrying only the target id and the time (Art. 5(2)), which a re-run does not redact. Erasure REFUSES while there is an active loan, a queued/ready hold or an outstanding fine, naming the counts. It is safe to repeat: the outbox purge and the photo delete run BEFORE the tombstone because both are keyed on data the tombstone destroys. DELETE still archives, on purpose, and both the controller header and the DELETE handler now say so and point at the erase route.

privacy-legal-05: `retention-sweep` is in SCHEDULED_JOBS (apps/api/src/jobs/retention.job.ts, 24h) — the registry the runner consumes — and the booted worker prints 10 jobs including `retention-sweep@86400s`. It enforces the only two periods this product actually states: (1) site applications at the 12 months libriant.com publishes in both languages (apps/site/content/privacy.{el,en}.md §5), keeping `accepted` rows because the same sentence says those details move into the library's account; (2) the tenant audit_log at the plan's `audit_log_retention_days`, resolved through EffectivePlanService — which with subscriptions OFF (the shipped configuration) resolves to the UNLIMITED sentinel, so the sweep deliberately deletes nothing there and says so. I did NOT invent periods for the other five stores the finding named: Privacy Policy §6 still reads `[30]` days, `[14]`-day backups, `[up to 5–10]` years and `[a limited period, e.g. 90 days]` — four placeholders, so there is nothing to enforce and guessing would put a deletion schedule nobody agreed to into production. That is reported below, not silently filled in.

Two things worth knowing. First, the first implementation of the tombstone 500'd against a real tenant database: `members_member_number_format` is `CHECK (~ '^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9_-]{1,29}$')` and `ERASED-<cuid>` is both lowercase and 32 characters (SQLSTATE 23514, patron's row left fully intact). That is why `erasedMemberNumber()` exists and why its comment is long. Second, for about 40 minutes the whole AppModule could not boot — another agent's in-flight `TenantPrismaService(role)` constructor was unresolvable by Nest DI and every integration spec in the suite died at `NestFactory.create`, mine included; they landed `@Optional() @Inject(TENANT_POOL_ROLE)` and the suite went green. No migration was needed: `members.erasedAt` already existed from the previous attempt, and my schema change is comment-only (verified: `prisma migrate deploy` twice on a scratch DB → "No pending migrations", `migrate status` → "Database schema is up to date").

findings_addressed.what_changed: Added MembersService.erase() + POST /t/:slug/members/:id/erase (@Roles('owner','admin')). Tombstones every identifier on the member row, deletes the photo file from storage, strips notes/customFields on Loan/Reservation/Fine and Fine.reason, redacts the tenant audit_log payloads for that member, purges control-plane email_outbox rows addressed to them, writes one identifier-free member.erased audit row. Refuses on open business; idempotent. Executed end-to-end over HTTP: after the call, 0 rows anywhere in the tenant database contain the patron's name, e-mail, street or staff note, the photo file is gone from the volume, the closed loan survives with notes=NULL.

Erasure does not reach the control-plane import residue (ImportBatch.columnsJson sample rows, ImportRowIssue.rawJson), which can hold the same patron's raw import row. A refused erase (open business detected under the lock) has already deleted that member's queued notices — the harmless direction, documented in the code.

findings_addressed.what_changed: Added apps/api/src/jobs/retention.job.ts and REGISTERED it in apps/api/src/jobs/registry.ts as `retention-sweep` @ 24h. Limb 1 deletes site applications 12 months after last contact (reviewedAt ?? createdAt), keeping status='accepted' — exactly what apps/site/content/privacy.{el,en}.md §5 publishes. Limb 2 deletes tenant audit_log rows past the plan's audit_log_retention_days, in bounded 5k batches, skipping tenants whose plan grants unlimited (the shipped posture) and refusing a retention < 1 day rather than wiping a library's audit log on a bad seed value. Per-tenant failures land in `tenantsFailed` so a broken tenant makes the run NOT ok on /healthz. Updated the tenant schema comment that claimed a background job existed when none did.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: PARTIAL because five of the six stores the finding named still have no enforceable period: control-plane audit_log, support_sessions / support_redemption_attempts (IP addresses), users.legalAcceptedIp and the email_outbox envelope all fall under Privacy Policy §6, whose four periods are still `[PLACEHOLDER]`s. I enforced nothing there rather than inventing numbers — the brief's own instruction. Each needs one limb once counsel fills §6 in. Also: the applications DELETE has no index that fits its predicate (applications has indexes on createdAt and (status, createdAt)); the table is tiny today, so this is a note, not a problem.

verdicts.reasoning: The audited defect no longer reproduces, and this time the code is really in the working tree (unlike the previous attempt, where `git diff -- apps/api/src/members/` was empty). `git diff` shows members.service.ts +366 (erase(), assertNoOpenBusiness(), redactAuditTrail(), erasedMemberNumber(), StorageService injected) and members.controller.ts +32 (`@Roles('owner','admin') @Post(':id/erase')` at line 164). I booted the API myself with NODE_ENV=production against the audit control DB: `Nest application successfully started`, `/healthz` 200, and the route table shows `Mapped {/t/:slug/members/:id/erase, POST}` alongside the untouched DELETE. I then ran the earlier verifier's exact repro over HTTP on a freshly signed-up tenant: created a member with fullName/email/phone/dateOfBirth/addressLine1-2/city/postalCode/country/staffNotes, checked a copy out and returned it with a note naming her, marked a second copy lost, uploaded a photo. `DELETE /t/:slug/members/:id` -> 200 and every field read back intact (archive, deliberate). `POST .../erase` -> 201 and the row reads memberNumber=ERASED-00009FMVMBD4JUTL, fullName='[erased]', email/dateOfBirth/addressLine1/staffNotes all NULL, erasedAt set. Crucially I did NOT trust their five-table sweep: I enumerated EVERY table in `pg_tables` for the tenant database and ran `SELECT count(*) FROM t x WHERE x::text ILIKE '%needle%'` for the name, e-mail, street and staff note — all four returned NONE across the whole database. The photo file was gone from /tmp/lbraudit/storage/<tenant>/members/. audit_log beforeJson/afterJson for the member became {"redacted":"member.erased"}, with one identifier-free `member.erased` row added. The closed loan survived. Re-running erase returned alreadyErased:true and did not duplicate or wipe the erasure record; GET and LIST still serve the tombstone. `apps/api/test/integration/retention-erasure.spec.ts` really does drive supertest against the routes (I watched the request log) — 8/8 pass — and `npx tsc --noEmit` in apps/api is clean. So the mechanism is genuine. BUT it ships with two holes I found by execution and am filing as new problems: (1) the refusal gate counts outstanding fines and the product has NO route or UI to pay or waive a fine, so erasure is permanently impossible for any member who ever went overdue — I had to `UPDATE fines SET status='waived'` in SQL to get past it; (2) the control-plane outbox purge is keyed on the member's CURRENT e-mail, so a notice sent to a previous address survives with her full name and the book title in it. Marking fixed because the audited defect (archive-only, no erasure path at all) is dead, not because the capability is complete.

The one thing the previous refutation named — registration — is genuinely done. I booted the real worker under NODE_ENV=production and it printed `[scheduled] started — 10 job(s): … retention-sweep@86400s`, ten where the earlier verifier counted nine. I drove the handler through the REGISTRY entry (`SCHEDULED_JOBS.find(j=>j.name==='retention-sweep').handler(ctx)`) with five seeded applications and limb 1 is correct and idempotent: run 1 deleted exactly the 13-month-old `new` row and the one reviewed 400 days ago, kept `accepted`, kept the one contacted 60 days ago, kept the 3-month-old one; run 2 deleted nothing. I verified the 12 months is real (apps/site/content/privacy.{el,en}.md) and that locales/en/legal/privacy.md §6 is still four literal placeholders — `[30]`, `[14]`, `[up to 5–10]`, `[a limited period, e.g. 90 days]` — so declining to invent periods there is the right call. Still NOT fixed, for three executed reasons. (a) Limb 2 is BROKEN for a real seeded plan. The code guards the sentinel with `isUnlimitedInt(days)` = `days >= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, but the product's own unlimited value is 1_000_000_000 — I confirmed it live: `select * from plan_feature_values where featureKey='audit_log_retention_days'` returns 7/90/365/1095/3650/1000000000, the last belonging to `on-prem-enterprise`. 1e9 passes both `isUnlimitedInt` and `Number.isFinite`, and `new Date(now - 1e9*86400000)` is **Invalid Date**. I put my test tenant on that plan with billing on and ran the registered handler: `retention sweep failed for tenant=vfy-stale-4558b5: Error: Invalid value for argument \`date\`: Provided Date object is invalid.` and `"tenantsFailed":2`. Per apps/api/src/jobs/jobs.types.ts a `…Failed` counter makes the run NOT ok on /healthz, so that tenant turns retention-sweep permanently red — the exact failure mode the comment above the guard claims to have prevented. (b) In the shipped posture (subscriptions off) limb 2 deletes nothing at all: my registry run reported `66 tenant(s) on unlimited retention — nothing to enforce`. So today exactly ONE of the six stores the finding named has an enforced period. (c) The concrete residue the previous refutation demonstrated is untouched: control-plane email_outbox still keeps the named patron plus the exact book title forever, and I proved it survives even a full member erasure (see new problems). control audit_log, support_sessions/support_redemption_attempts IPs and users.legalAcceptedIp are likewise untouched. The implementer self-reported this as `partial` and that is the honest label; the finding is not closed.

new_problems.issue: Erasure refuses while the member has an outstanding fine, and the product ships no way to clear one. There is no fines controller anywhere in apps/api/src (no @Controller for fines, no waive/pay/settle route; `grep -rn "fines" apps/api/src --include=*.controller.ts` returns only comments, and apps/web has no fines UI). The only code paths that move a fine off `outstanding` are the automatic waiver inside loans.service.ts:518 when overdue fines are disabled at return, and the CSV import engine. So any member who ever went overdue (fine-accrual.job creates those automatically) or was billed for a lost book can never be erased through the product — the Art. 17 capability is unavailable to exactly the patrons most likely to invoke it, and the 400's own text ("settle or waive the fines first") instructs the librarian to do something the software cannot do. This is the out-of-band-SQL state the finding condemned, just moved one step later.
new_problems.reproduction: Booted the API with NODE_ENV=production on :9393. Signed up tenant vfy-erase-e6a15d, created a member, checked out a copy and `POST /loans/:id/mark-lost {replacementCostCents:1500}` -> 201 with a fine. `POST /t/vfy-erase-e6a15d/members/<id>/erase` -> 400 {"message":"Can't erase a member with open business…","activeLoans":0,"activeReservations":0,"outstandingFines":1}. I then had to run `UPDATE fines SET status='waived' WHERE "memberId"=$1` directly in Postgres before the erase would return 201 — there is no HTTP route that does this.

new_problems.issue: The control-plane email_outbox purge is keyed on `toEmail: existing.email`, i.e. the member's CURRENT address only. Members can and do change their e-mail via PATCH, and notices already sent to the old address survive erasure carrying the patron's full name in bodyMarkdown and the borrowed book's title in the subject, in the SHARED control plane, forever (no retention limb covers email_outbox — privacy-legal-05 is still partial). Worse, the same call redacts the tenant audit_log rows that held the old address, so afterwards nothing links the surviving row back to the erased member and no future sweep can find it. The report's claim that erase "deletes control-plane email_outbox rows addressed to them" is only true for the address they happen to hold at the moment of erasure.

Created member 'Ελένη Στέιλ-4558b5' with email old.4558b5@patron.test; inserted a delivered member_overdue outbox row to that address (subject «Εκπρόθεσμο: «Το Κιβώτιο» (4558b5)», body 'Αγαπητή Ελένη Στέιλ-4558b5, …', tenantId set) exactly as member-notifications.job writes them; `PATCH /members/:id {email:new.4558b5@patron.test}` -> 200; inserted a second notice to the new address. `POST /members/:id/erase` -> 201 with cleared.outboxMessages=1. email_outbox afterwards still contains toEmail=old.4558b5@patron.test with bodyMarkdown='Αγαπητή Ελένη Στέιλ-4558b5, το βιβλίο έχει λήξει.'

new_problems.issue: The unlimited-retention guard only recognises `days >= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, but the plan the product actually seeds as unlimited (`on-prem-enterprise`) carries audit_log_retention_days = 1_000_000_000. That value passes both `isUnlimitedInt` and the `Number.isFinite(days) && days >= 1` check, and `new Date(now - 1e9 * 86_400_000)` overflows the JS Date range to Invalid Date. Prisma rejects it, the per-tenant catch increments `tenantsFailed`, and per apps/api/src/jobs/jobs.types.ts a `…Failed` counter makes the run NOT ok — so a single tenant on the top plan turns retention-sweep permanently red on /healthz, every day, hiding any real failure behind it. The long comment on the guard claims to have handled exactly this case.
new_problems.reproduction: `select * from plan_feature_values where "featureKey"='audit_log_retention_days'` -> 7, 90, 365, 1095, 3650, 1000000000 (last = on-prem-enterprise). Resolved it live: EffectivePlanService.getInt(tenant,'audit_log_retention_days') = 1000000000 with billing on; `new Date(Date.now()-1000000000*86400000)` = Invalid Date. Put tenant vfy-stale-4558b5 on that plan (status active, paidUntil future), set platform_setting billing.enabled=true, flushed the plan cache, and ran SCHEDULED_JOBS.find(j=>j.name==='retention-sweep').handler(ctx): `[RetentionSweep] retention sweep failed for tenant=vfy-stale-4558b5: Error: Invalid value for argument \`date\`: Provided Date object is invalid.` and result counts {"auditRowsDeleted":0,"tenantsUnlimited":0,"tenantsFailed":2}. findings_addressed.what_changed: apps/api/src/export/export-processors.ts. (1) `approxRowBytes` rewritten: it now recursively walks arrays and plain objects (parsed jsonb, composites, ranges) instead of charging them a flat 16 bytes, counts Buffers/TypedArrays/Dates/bigints, and — the important half — charges an un-walkable value (past a 20,000-node walk budget) the FULL FETCH budget, so truncation collapses the batch instead of silently under-counting it. (2) New `widestRowBytes()` + exported `tableRowCeiling()`: before the cursor is DECLAREd, one server-side aggregate measures the widest row in the table and `readTableInBatches` clamps rows-per-FETCH to `budgetBytes / (widest * 2)`. That bounds the FIRST batch, which is the hole bypass B fell through — any bound derived from rows already read cannot see a wide tail. The probe expression is assembled per column from pg_attribute so it is cheap: fixed-width types contribute typlen with no I/O, text/varchar/bytea use octet_length() which reads the uncompressed size out of the TOAST pointer without fetching a chunk (1.46 ms on the 80 MB wide probe vs 22.3 s for octet_length(t::text)), and only json/jsonb/arrays pay a serialization. It runs with its own 10-minute statement_timeout inside the export's REPEATABLE READ snapshot and, if it fails, falls SMALL (64 rows) rather than open.

fix.summary:
billing-03: the verifier's window (Stripe delivers `checkout.session.completed` BEFORE `customer.subscription.created`, so our row reads null and the marker is already consumed) is closed by two guards. DURABLE — `handleCheckoutSessionCompleted` now writes `stripeSubscriptionId` to Postgres from `payload.subscription` (via `updateMany where stripeSubscriptionId: null`, so it can never clobber a tracked id) BEFORE it drops the Redis marker, and keeps the marker when there is no id to write. AUTHORITATIVE — with no id on the row, `startCheckout` asks Stripe what subscriptions the CUSTOMER has (new `StripeDriver.listSubscriptions`, `subscriptions.list({status:'all'})`) and adopts + re-prices a live one instead of selling a second; this also covers a flushed Redis, a lost webhook, and a marker deleted any other way. It cannot brick purchasing: no live subscription at Stripe → Checkout opens as before; Stripe unreachable → 503 "try again", never a second subscription; no Stripe customer yet → zero extra API calls; the adopted pointer is re-verified (and cleared when dead) by the existing `resolveLiveSubscription`. Also fixed in passing: the re-price path called `discardCheckoutMarker` under a comment saying completing that session "WOULD produce" a second subscription — it now calls `expireOutstandingCheckout`, which revokes the session AT Stripe and keeps the marker if the revoke fails so the next attempt retries.

reliability-16: the third cause was real. `stripe-retry.job.ts:130` picked its driver with `env.stripeDriver === 'real' ? new RealStripeDriver() : new FakeStripeDriver()`, bypassing the posture factory; `config/env.ts` maps the shipped `STRIPE_DRIVER=none` to `'real'` outside development, so every tick built RealStripeDriver with no API key and threw. The sweep now resolves the posture with `resolveStripeDriverKind()` and builds through `createStripeDriver()`. And the honest answer for `disabled` IS "the sweep cannot and should not run": the webhook route answers 503 before reading a body in that posture, so nothing can enter the retry set, and replaying stored payloads would make this sweep the only writer of subscription rows on a host that deliberately switched that path off. So it returns early — ok, explicit, with the held pile counted in the message and in `counts.held` — instead of failing 288 times a day. It still retries for real when Stripe is configured. The sweep also gained the `checkout.session.completed` case its dispatch was silently dropping into `default` (i.e. marking processed without doing anything) — that is the handler billing-03's durable guard depends on — and now passes Redis into BillingService.

findings_addressed.what_changed: billing.service.ts: handleCheckoutSessionCompleted writes the subscription id durably before dropping the marker (and keeps the marker when the payload has none); startCheckout consults Stripe about the CUSTOMER via the new adoptCustomerSubscription() when our row has no id, and re-prices instead of opening a second Checkout; the re-price path now expires the outstanding session at Stripe (expireOutstandingCheckout) instead of forgetting it. stripe-driver.ts + real/fake/disabled drivers gained listSubscriptions(customerId).
findings_addressed.residual_risk: adoptCustomerSubscription picks liveOnes[0], relying on Stripe returning list results newest-first (documented behaviour, not verifiable here — every price id is a price_seed_* placeholder and BILLING_ENABLED is false, so no call ever hit api.stripe.com). If a customer somehow has two live subscriptions, we re-price one and log an error naming both rather than refusing; that is deliberate (refusing cannot un-bill the second) but needs an operator to cancel the extra in Stripe. The one window left is sub-second: both Checkout sessions still OPEN at Stripe when the second click lands — that is what the Redis marker + expire covers, and an expire that fails mid-completion still fails closed with a 409.

findings_addressed.what_changed: stripe-retry.job.ts now resolves the Stripe posture with resolveStripeDriverKind() and builds the driver with createStripeDriver() instead of a hand-rolled ternary. The 'disabled' posture returns an explicit ok result ('billing is switched off (STRIPE_DRIVER=none) — … nothing to retry; N event(s) … held') with counts {retried:0, held:N}; 'held' is not a *Failed key, so the run stays green on the health surface while the pile is still visible. checkout.session.completed added to the sweep's dispatch; Redis is passed to BillingService.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: Rows captured while billing was on are HELD, not retried, for as long as STRIPE_DRIVER=none. They drain on the first tick after billing is switched back on, and the count is printed every 5 minutes — but an operator who never re-enables billing will see a permanent non-zero 'held'. That is the intended signal, not a failure.

new_problems.issue: A Checkout session that completes into an `incomplete` subscription (delayed-notification payment methods such as SEPA Direct Debit / Bacs) consumes BOTH duplicate-purchase guards and still lets a second subscription be sold. handleCheckoutSessionCompleted only keeps the marker when `payload.subscription` is ABSENT; when the id is present but the subscription is not yet live it writes the pointer and deletes the marker anyway (:1099). On the next click resolveLiveSubscription clears the pointer (incomplete is deliberately not in STRIPE_LIVE_STATUSES) and adoptCustomerSubscription filters the same subscription out, so startCheckout falls through to a fresh Checkout. If the delayed payment later clears, the customer holds two live subscriptions — the finding's own failure mode, reached by a different door.
new_problems.reproduction: EXECUTED against real Postgres + real Redis (probe S8d): open Checkout for Community, complete it into a subscription whose Stripe status is `incomplete`, deliver checkout.session.completed, then click Municipal. Observed: 'S8d after completed: row = {stripeSubscriptionId: sub_cs_1} marker = null'; then WARN 'still pointed at Stripe subscription sub_cs_1 (status incomplete) — clearing the pointer and treating this as a fresh purchase'; 'S8d -> checkout | sessions = 2 [cs_2:open, cs_1:complete] | subs = [sub_cs_1:incomplete]'. Flip sub_cs_1 to active (the SEPA debit clears) and two live subscriptions exist. NOT a regression — HEAD behaves the same or worse — and unreachable with card Checkout, where a completed session means the payment already cleared. The narrow fix is to keep the marker whenever the completed session's subscription is not in STRIPE_LIVE_STATUSES, exactly as the no-subscription-id branch above it already does.

new_problems.issue: expireOutstandingCheckout reads the marker with a bare `this.redis.client.get(key).catch(() => null)`, which fails OPEN: a Redis outage is indistinguishable from 'no session outstanding', so the re-price path silently skips revoking a still-completable Checkout session at Stripe. Every other read on this guard goes through redisCall(), which fails CLOSED with a 503 precisely because the thing being guarded is a duplicate live subscription. The asymmetry is undocumented in the function's otherwise thorough comment, which explains only the expire-refusal case.
new_problems.reproduction: Read-verified, not executed (it needs Redis to fail between the re-price and the expire). Sequence: tenant has a live subscription AND an open Checkout session recorded in the marker; Redis goes down; the tenant clicks another plan; startCheckout re-prices, expireOutstandingCheckout's GET rejects, `.catch(() => null)` returns null, the function returns having revoked nothing, and the still-open session at Stripe remains completable for its full 24h. Strictly better than HEAD, which called discardCheckoutMarker and never expired anything at all — so this is a residual, not a regression.
